standard: UK Acute Upper GI Bleeding (AUGIB) care bundle (BSG Endoscopy Quality Improvement Project), following the 2015 NCEPOD report
finding: Glasgow Blatchford Score recorded in 38.4% (163/459); target haemoglobin stated in 35.3%; transfusion threshold appropriate in 13.3%; rebleeding plan documented in 33.2%.
change: Implementation of the UK AUGIB care bundle, with a period of bundle promotion between data collection cycles.

cycle1.result: Glasgow Blatchford Score recorded in 38.4% (163/459); target haemoglobin stated in 35.3%; transfusion threshold appropriate in 13.3%; rebleeding plan documented in 33.2%.

detail.intervention: Implementation of the UK AUGIB care bundle, with a period of bundle promotion between data collection cycles.

cycle2.result: Glasgow Blatchford Score recorded in 57.3% (225/434, p<0.001); target haemoglobin stated in 44.8%; transfusion threshold appropriate in 19.6% (p=0.012); rebleeding plan documented in 50.7% (p<0.001); the bundle was used in 41.2% of patients.

detail.other_findings: No significant differences found in PPI use for high-risk bleeders, terlipressin/antibiotics for variceal haemorrhage, or antithrombotic resumption plan, which were already high pre-bundle.

title: PWE-082 The art of combining clinical intuition and nuclear medicine in diagnosing bile acid malabsorption
topic: SeHCAT scanning for bile acid malabsorption
standard: NICE DG7 (2012); 2018 BSG guidelines for investigation of chronic diarrhoea
finding: 49.8% of patients had an abnormal SeHCAT test; testing volume increased from 26/year to 124/year over 5 years; of 2,476 post-cholecystectomy patients, 64 developed diarrhoea, of whom 41 (64%) tested positive.

cycle1.result: 49.8% of patients had an abnormal SeHCAT test; testing volume increased from 26/year to 124/year over 5 years; of 2,476 post-cholecystectomy patients, 64 developed diarrhoea, of whom 41 (64%) tested positive.

detail.other_findings: No symptom 'hallmark' identified for bile acid malabsorption despite a high pick-up rate by experienced clinicians; supports the BSG guideline audit recommendation of SeHCAT use in IBS-D as a quality improvement target.

title: PTU-75 A Clinical Audit of Severity Assessment of Acute Pancreatitis using scoring systems
topic: Severity assessment scoring in acute pancreatitis
standard: not reported (scoring systems referenced, e.g. APACHE II; no named numeric target)
finding: At one centre 33% of patients were scored using APACHE II; at two other centres this rose to 77.8% and 33.3%; for all scored patients there was 0% ITU admission or mortality.
